# tidylayouts

The goal of `tidylayouts` is to streamline the creation of multi-plot
layouts for scientific papers. It allows to gradually expand and adjust
layouts using a consistent and intuitive syntax.

`tidylayouts` is built around the pipe and supports plots with absolute
dimensions, such as those created with `tidyplots`, as well as plain
`ggplot2` plots. Plots are aligned by their **panels**, not by their
outer boxes, so axes and tags line up across the whole figure.

## Installation

You can install the development version from
[GitHub](https://github.com/) with:

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("jbengler/tidylayouts")
```

## Usage

Build a figure step by step:
[`new_row()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/new_row.md)
adds a row of plots below everything so far,
[`new_column()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/new_row.md)
adds a column to the right.

``` r

library(tidylayouts)

new_row(p1, p2) |>
  new_row(p3, p4) |>
  new_column(auto_height(p5)) |>
  new_column(auto_height(p6)) |>
  new_row(auto_width(p7))
```

![](reference/figures/README-usage-dummies-1.png)

All plots above have a fixed panel size of 30 × 30 mm.
[`auto_height()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/auto_width.md)
and
[`auto_width()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/auto_width.md)
let the layout decide the panel size: the panel fills the space it gets
from its neighbours: `p5` and `p6` span the height of the block on the
left, `p7` spans the width of everything above.

[`new_grid()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/new_row.md)
adds a block of plots that share rows and columns.

## Real plots

``` r

tidyplots_options(
  width = 25,
  height = 25,
  my_style = function(x) x |> remove_legend()
)

p1 <- study |>
  tidyplot(x = group, y = score, color = dose) |>
  add_mean_bar(alpha = 0.3) |>
  add_sem_errorbar() |>
  add_data_points() |>
  add_test_asterisks(hide_info = TRUE)
p2 <- time_course |>
  tidyplot(x = day, y = score, color = treatment, dodge_width = 0) |>
  add_mean_line() |>
  add_sem_ribbon()
p3 <- energy_week |>
  tidyplot(x = date, y = power, color = energy_source) |>
  add_areastack_relative()
p4 <- energy |>
  tidyplot(y = energy, color = energy_source) |>
  add_donut()
p5 <- climate |>
  tidyplot(x = month, y = year, color = max_temperature) |>
  add_heatmap() |>
  adjust_size(height = 55)
p6 <- gene_expression |>
  tidyplot(x = sample, y = external_gene_name, color = expression) |>
  add_heatmap(scale = "row") |>
  sort_y_axis_labels(direction, -padj) |>
  adjust_size(height = 55) |>
  remove_x_axis_title() |>
  remove_y_axis_title()
p7 <- gene_expression |>
  head(100) |>
  tidyplot(x = sample_type, y = expression, color = condition) |>
  add_violin() |>
  add_data_points_beeswarm(white_border = TRUE) |>
  adjust_x_axis_title("") |>
  add_test_asterisks(hide_info = TRUE, bracket.nudge.y = 0.3) |>
  adjust_y_axis_title("Gene expression") |>
  split_plot(by = external_gene_name, nrow = 1)

tidyplots_options()
```

By default, plots keep their size. In a row, panels are aligned at the
bottom so that the x axes line up. The panel tags are still aligned at
the top of the row.

``` r

new_row(p1, p2) |>
  new_row(p3, p4) |>
  new_column(p5) |>
  new_column(p6) |>
  new_row(p7) |>
  layout_tags("A")
```

![](reference/figures/README-real-fixed-1.png)

Freeing the heatmaps and the violin plots makes them fill the available
space.

``` r

new_row(p1, p2) |>
  new_row(p3, p4) |>
  new_column(auto_height(p5)) |>
  new_column(auto_height(p6)) |>
  new_row(auto_width(p7)) |>
  layout_tags("A")
```

![](reference/figures/README-real-freed-1.png)

## Design strings

[`new_layout()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/new_layout.md)
describes a whole figure in one call. Each letter in the design is a
plot; plots are assigned in alphabetical order of the letters, and `#`
marks an empty cell.

``` r

new_layout(
  tag_group(p1, p2), p3, p4, p5, p6, p7,
  design = "
    ABEF
    CDEF
    GGGG
  ",
  auto_width = "G",
  auto_height = "EF",
  auto_margins_x = "D",
  tags = "A"
)
```

![](reference/figures/README-design-1.png)

By default, each line of the design becomes a row, so the figure above
has the same structure as
`new_row(p1, p2) |> new_row(p3, p4) |> new_column(p5) |> new_column(p6) |> new_row(p7)`.
With `arrange_by = "column"`, each design column becomes a column
instead, and with `arrange_by = "grid"` plots in the same row and column
of the design share their lines.

The design shows the arrangement, not the size: plots keep their panel
sizes, also when they span several cells. `auto_width`, `auto_height`,
`auto_margins_x` and `auto_margins_y` change that for the listed plots,
like the functions
[`auto_width()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/auto_width.md),
[`auto_height()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/auto_width.md)
and
[`auto_margins()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/auto_width.md).
Tags are numbered in reading order, as with
[`layout_tags()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/layout_size.md);
here
[`tag_group()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/tag_group.md)
lets the first two plots share tag A.

## Alignment

Plots with a fixed size often leave some space in their row or column.
`horizontal_align` and `vertical_align` decide where it goes. The
defaults are `"left"` and `"bottom"`, where the axis lines are.

``` r

new_row(p1, p2)
```

![](reference/figures/README-align-1.png)

``` r

new_row(p1, p2, vertical_align = "top")
```

![](reference/figures/README-align-2.png)

``` r

new_row(p1, p2, vertical_align = "center")
```

![](reference/figures/README-align-3.png)

``` r

new_column(p1, p3, horizontal_align = "center")
```

![](reference/figures/README-align-column-1.png)

Alignment applies to what is directly inside a row or column. A nested
row fills the width it is given and arranges its own plots, e.g. with
the extra space between them:

``` r

new_row(p3, p3) |>
  new_row(p1, p1, horizontal_align = "justify")
```

![](reference/figures/README-align-nested-1.png)

To center a single plot within the spare space next to it, use
[`auto_margins()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/auto_width.md).
The panel keeps its size, the extra space goes to both sides, and the
tag stays at the edge of the space. Use `y = FALSE` to center only
horizontally, so the plot keeps the row’s shared bottom edge.

``` r

new_row(p3, p3) |>
  new_row(p1, auto_margins(p1, y = FALSE)) |>
  layout_tags("A")
```

![](reference/figures/README-center-1.png)

## Rows of plots vs. grids

[`new_row()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/new_row.md)
lays out each row independently.
[`new_grid()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/new_row.md)
shares row and column tracks, so plots in the same grid column line up
exactly.

``` r

new_row(narrow, narrow) |> new_row(wide, wide)
```

![](reference/figures/README-grid-1.png)

``` r

new_grid(narrow, narrow, wide, wide, ncol = 2)
```

![](reference/figures/README-grid-2.png)

## Wrapping rows

`new_row(..., wrap = <mm>)` breaks a long row into lines, like text in a
word processor: each line takes as many plots as fit, axis labels and
gaps included. This is handy when plots have different widths.

``` r

new_row(panels, wrap = 140, horizontal_align = "justify") |>
  layout_tags("A")
```

![](reference/figures/README-wrap-1.png)

With `horizontal_align = "justify"`, all lines but the last are spread
to the width of the widest line.

`new_column(..., wrap = <mm>)` does the same vertically: a column that
is too tall continues in a new column to the right, like newspaper
columns.

For plots of similar width, such as small multiples,
`new_grid(..., wrap = <mm>)` picks as many grid columns as fit. All rows
share the same columns, so the plots line up in both directions.

``` r

small <- lapply(1:7, function(i) dummy(width = 30, height = 20, name = paste0("p", i), color = cols[i]))

new_grid(small, wrap = 120) |>
  layout_tags("A")
```

![](reference/figures/README-wrap-grid-1.png)

## Layout options

``` r

new_row(narrow, wide) |>
  new_row(auto_width(narrow)) |>
  layout_tags("a") |>
  layout_title("Figure 1") |>
  layout_size(width = 120)
```

![](reference/figures/README-options-1.png)

To let several plots share one tag, wrap them in
[`tag_group()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/tag_group.md).
Only the first plot of the group gets a tag, and the sequence continues
after the group.

``` r

tag_group(new_row(narrow, wide)) |>
  new_row(auto_width(narrow)) |>
  layout_tags("A")
```

![](reference/figures/README-tag-group-1.png)

By default, the gaps between plots come from each plot’s own margins.
[`layout_spacing()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/layout_size.md)
replaces them with fixed gaps in mm, so spacing stays even when plots
use different themes. `inner` takes one value for both directions or
`c(horizontal, vertical)`; `outer` adds a margin around the whole
figure.

``` r

new_row(narrow, wide) |>
  new_row(auto_width(narrow)) |>
  layout_tags("a") |>
  layout_spacing(inner = c(2, 6), outer = 5)
```

![](reference/figures/README-spacing-1.png)

Save a figure at its exact physical size with
[`save_layout()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/save_layout.md).
If all panels have a fixed size, the figure size is computed from the
layout.

``` r

save_layout(my_layout, "figure1.pdf")
save_layout(my_layout, "figure1.pdf", width = 183)  # Nature double column
```

## Placeholders

[`dummy()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/dummy.md)
creates placeholder plots for sketching layouts.
[`spacer()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/dummy.md)
creates an empty slot: with a size in mm it is a fixed gap, without a
size it absorbs leftover space.

``` r

new_row(p1, spacer(width = 20), p1)
```

![](reference/figures/README-placeholders-1.png)

``` r

new_row(p1, spacer(), p1) |> layout_size(width = 150)
```

![](reference/figures/README-placeholders-2.png)

# Package index

## Create

Create a new layout by combining rows, columns and grids, or start from
a design string.

- [`new_row()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/new_row.md)
  [`new_column()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/new_row.md)
  [`new_grid()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/new_row.md)
  : Build a layout row by row
- [`new_layout()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/new_layout.md)
  : Lay out plots from a design string

## Size and margins

Modify sizes a margins of individual plots.

- [`auto_width()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/auto_width.md)
  [`auto_height()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/auto_width.md)
  [`auto_margins()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/auto_width.md)
  [`set_size()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/auto_width.md)
  : Panel sizes and margins in a layout

## Adjust

Adjust layout properties.

- [`layout_size()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/layout_size.md)
  [`layout_spacing()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/layout_size.md)
  [`layout_tags()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/layout_size.md)
  [`layout_title()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/layout_size.md)
  : Layout options
- [`tag_group()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/tag_group.md)
  : Share one tag among several plots

## Save

- [`save_layout()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/save_layout.md)
  : Save a layout

## Placeholders

- [`dummy()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/dummy.md)
  [`spacer()`](https://jbengler.github.io/tidylayouts/reference/dummy.md)
  : Placeholders
